surfaces.part: lava rock heap upper mass (mottled gray plates with red ember specks)
dark underside / shadowed lower edge of heap

answer.evidence: Irregular low heap of rock plates. Rows 4-19 are mid-gray with lighter highlight rows (L=114 at rows 14-15 in the scan) and read as a heap seen from above, which is evidence (d). Rows 20-26 are a very dark band (L=17-20) that narrows from width 25 to 4, so the heap has a shadowed front/underside face of about 6 rows. It is not a flat top-down slab and not a flat elevation. The kind (debris) matches the scattered rock pile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small rock-like lava prop of about 1.5 tiles. It has about 9 visible tones per tile, which matches the hedge but sits well below the well (20) and the stall (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat fills, and the rock facets show some light/dark variation with a few ember-red accents. The weak point is the outline: 86% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, and the picture shows a near-black rim around the whole silhouette. That is the uniform sticker-style line, not the dark material tone Beodeul uses (the hedge has 0% neutral edges, the stall 1%). The main rock body has only about 3-4 grey steps, shallower than the 5-6 on the references, and the texture is limited to a few speckles and cracks. Overall it is clean and not flat, but the near-black outline and the shallower ramps keep it below the Beodeul bar.

surfaces.part: cooled lava crust mass (flat irregular plates with cracks)
dark underside / cast shadow at the bottom edge

answer.evidence: The object is a low, irregular, flat patch of lava plates with red cracks and no upright volume. Rows 4-21 are one broad surface seen from above, with the width growing from 16 to 29 and then tapering. There is no front-edge line followed by an eave shadow. Rows 22-26 are a tapering dark shadow or underside, not a vertical south face of 3 or more rows. This fits flat floor debris, so it reads as a top-down slab and not as a three-quarter volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small dark rock lump with red lava veins, about 9 visible tones per tile. That matches the hedge but sits well below the well (20) and the cheese stall (17). Shading has roughly 4 steps on the rock: a lighter grey-blue top, mid and dark planes, and red/orange cracks. The outline is a near-black, almost neutral rim. 86% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the hedge and stall, which have tinted outlines. This reads as a sticker-like dark silhouette rather than a dark tone of the adjacent material. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills, and the rock facets carry some texture. Even so, it is thinner and flatter than the richer references (well, stall) and its outline is neutral, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.

surfaces.part: cooled lava rubble mass (irregular rock chunks with red glowing cracks)

answer.evidence: The object is a flat scattering of irregular rock fragments, with a silhouette about 24-29 px wide and about 20 rows tall (rows 4-26). It is lying debris, not a standing volume. The column scans show alternating light and dark runs with no consistent front-edge line or eave shadow. Light pixels appear at rows 4-7, 10, 11, 14, 15, 19 and 20. These are individual chunk highlights and do not form a band across the body. Red glowing cracks are sparse single pixels. The dark base at rows 22-26 is a cast shadow tapering from 22 to 4 px wide, not a vertical front face. The kind is debris, so the object has no box-like structure and reads as a flat top-down scatter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small rock-like lava mound with red glowing cracks. It has about 4 grey lightness steps plus a few red ember tones. The dark edge pixels are 86% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral near-black line. The Beodeul references use tinted dark tones (hedge 0%, cheese stall 1%). Visible tones per tile are 9, the same as the hedge but well below the well (20) and the stall (17). There are no flat fills (0% near-flat). Texture is only moderate: the facets are shaded, but there is little grain or per-stone dotting. The neutral outline gives it a slight sticker look next to the references, and the small tone count keeps it below the richer props. Overall it is acceptable on structure but shallower than the Beodeul standard, so it fails under the when-in-doubt rule.
